text_fidelity_a:
Polk Audio ES35 Sound Wall Mount Speakers, Black & Polk Audio ES15 Wall Mount Bookshelf Speaker, Black I'm very pleased with all aspects of this center speaker. The sound quality is excellent. This replaces an old KEF center speaker and the difference can be clearly heard. The Polk has a crisp, clean sound that clarifies and enhances dialog but not at the expense of a nice solid bass (although I also have a subwoofer in the setup).

Aesthetically it's a simple, clean design. Normally I don't pay much attention to the look of a speaker but in this case, since it's a center speaker, it's in my line of sight all the time. It's about as unobtrusive you can get with a center speaker without compromising sound quality and performance. Polk did an excellent job with the design.

I looked at the new version of this (the ES35) and, while there are some small incremental improvements, I didn't consider them to be worth the extra $100 it costs. Plus, this was on a price dip for the differential between the two was $150, making this the clear choice.

While I have been partial to KEF in the past for speakers, the performance of this Polk has really wow'd me. At present I'm using this center speaker with KEF left and right front speakers, and KEF for surround. I've been so impressed with the ES35 that I'll be changing to Polk for my L/R soon, and keep the KEF only for surround (5.1.2 setup).

An excellent center speaker that hits the mark on all counts. Five stars.
text_fidelity_b: Polk Audio ES35 Sound Wall Mount Speakers, Black & Polk Audio ES15 Wall Mount Bookshelf Speaker, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Altec Lansing iMW555-BLK Inmotion Bluetooth Speaker Beyond the way it looks, it's relatively easy to pair via Bluetooth, you can charge your phone via USB or NFC, the wireless near-field connection scheme. I'd have given a tooth for an external speaker like this back in the 80s, when battery-powered speakers for the Sony Walkman existed. It's more than adequate for a dorm room or office space, it's lightweight, it seems to be pretty durable, each of the EIGHT speakers have a metal screen protecting the cones. CX -- No, I was wrong, there are NOT eight speakers, there are FOUR speakers, plus four extra cones which amplify the sound. I counted the grilles and assumed they were all speakers. My error!

This comes in a beautiful package, it would make a fantastic gift. It promises up to 8-10 hours of play, which is more than decent. There's a Mic In jack, which I'm somewhat baffled by, and an Aux jack, which is very handy if you own an older non-Bluetooth iPod. There's a Talk button for use with your phone. I'm unclear how that would function. This can be mounted on a wall, AND THEY INCLUDED THE WALL ANCHORS AND SCREWS. Very thoughtful.

The main thing, the sound quality, is better than I've heard with other Bluetooth speaker solutions, which, honestly, is not saying that much. I'm looking for a software EQ on my iPhone and I don't find one. I don't want to ask for the Moon, but an EQ on the speaker would be worth more to me than the NFC charging scheme.

A very good Bluetooth speaker solution. It looks gorgeous, it's easily paired, the sound is relatively bright and clear. Room-filling sound. It won't replace home stereos, but that's not what it's meant to do. Anyone young enough to NOT remember how good vinyl LPs sound will be positively thrilled with this device!

---

This device actually sounds better filling a room with sound than it does just sitting on your desk. For whatever that's worth. It sounds better if it's not right under your nose.

---

This device does match up with my iPhone very well, and without a lot of fuss or headaches like other Bluetooth solutions I've tried. If I can't get each device to sniff one another's butt, I lose interest pretty quickly. This device matches up on its own and easily, so that's a major plus.
text_fidelity_b: Altec Lansing iMW555-BLK Inmotion Bluetooth Speaker

Cable Matters DisplayPort to DVI Adapter (DP to DVI Adapter) My desktop computer has a built in graphics card on the motherboard and I added a graphics card for gaming. The graphics card has a DVI, VGA and DisplayPort outputs. I had two monitors hooked up, one to the DVI, and one to the VGA port. I had another monitor (actually a TV) which duplicated screen two using a splitter. But I wanted to use it as a third separate monitor.

I tried several things to make a third monitor work: a DVI to HDMI cable (not an active cable) didn't work - the computer never saw the third monitor. I also tried the built in graphics card on the motherboard, plugging in an HDMI cable to its port and connecting the TV. That didn't work. it seems only one graphics card can be enabled at a time; either the one on the motherboard, or the installed graphics card.

This worked. As soon as I plugged it in, going from the displayport on the graphics card to the HDMI cable, the computer saw & recognized the 3rd monitor. Now I have three separate monitors.

text_fidelity_a:
Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black) Taken for what this is supposed to be, this is a fabulous machine. It's not a primary computer. It's not a laptop replacement. If you need a low power/ultra-portable computer, go with a netbook.

This is more of a mutt. It's a portable media player that doesn't have as much storage as an iPod or a Zen, but has a larger, higher quality screen and a kickstand, which makes it easier to watch movies at a desk.

It can read ebooks. It's not quite as light or comfortable for long term reading as a Kindle, but it can support full color images. It's far superior for this purpose than any of the other devices Amazon has put out an app for.

It can run Windows 7. It's not a full powered machine, but it's even smaller than a netbook.

It fits a slot somewhere between a PDA/smartphone and a netbook, and it's brilliant.

I would have liked a larger hard drive, an SD card (it would have gotten 5 stars if it had one) and more than one USB slot. There is no ethernet port. It only connects wirelessly. The optional port replicator gives you Ethernet and two more USB slots, but still no SD.

A few things to keep in mind. When you're first setting it up, you can't access the virtual keyboard button, so you need to use the Ease of Access icon to get to that. Windows will say to press the space bar to activate the feature. Use the mouse click button (marked +).

The design is very sleek. It's comfortable to hold and work with. The screen has an adjustable brightness, which is easier on the eyes, and easier to use in bright sunlight. The low glare screen helps with this as well.

Overall, this is bleeding edge, early adopter technology.
text_fidelity_b: Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
HP Sprocket Portable Color Photo Printer, Print Social Media Photos on 2x3" Sticky-Backed Paper - Black (X7N08A) This is a great improvement over an earlier-gen ZINK paper ("zero ink") portable printer we have, which requires a wired connection and a proprietary charger, and no longer holds a charge well.

The HP Sprocket connects and prints wirelessly, charges from a standard micro-USB cable, and has a lithium-ion battery which is sure to last a lot longer.

We had it unboxed and printing in less than 5 minutes. You run it from a free app available for Android or Apple iOS devices. We used the Android version and it works great.

It takes less than 30 seconds to wirelessly send and print a photo. The prints are 2 inches by 3 inches, smooth and glossy, good resolution, and have a peel-and-stick backing for quick and easy mounting. In the long run, the priciest thing about a ZINK printer is the paper, so shop around for deals.

The prints came out a little to the warm side in color when sent "as is," but the app allows a lot of enhancement and has lots of effects you can add.

The Sprocket printer itself measures only 3 inches by 5 inches and less than an inch thick, and weighs about 6-and-a-half ounces. It's very portable.

And it's loads of fun.
text_fidelity_b: HP Sprocket Portable Color Photo Printer, Print Social Media Photos on 2x3" Sticky-Backed Paper - Black (X7N08A)

text_fidelity_a:
Seagate FreeAgent Go 320 GB USB 2.0 Portable External Hard Drive ST903203FAA2E1-RK (Black) I've been using an external Seagate drive for a few years for my daily backups, and it's worked great. However, it's not very portable (about the size of a thick paperback) and needs AC power. So, looked at what Seagate offers in a smaller size, and came across the FreeAgent Go.

It got good reviews in the computer mags and, after using it for a few days, I don't have a single complaint. It's tiny - very easy to toss into a laptop bag. It's powered from the USB port, so there's no need for a separate power connector or bulky transformer.

The included cable is pretty short -- bit over a foot long (didn't measure it - just a ballpark guess). I also bought the docking station which includes a much longer cable that has two connectors. I've not had any problems running the drive off my Dell Vostro with just a single connecter, but the double connector would come in hand should your PC not provide sufficient power over a single USB port. The docking station also comes with a carry case for the drive. Nothing fancy, but it's padded to help the drive survive being tossed about.

I have not installed any of the included software (looks like there's some backup and file synch software, plus encryption stuff). I'm using other software for that, so drive installation consisted of plugging it into a USB port, waiting a second for the PC to recognize it, then it's ready to go. About as easy as it gets!

The lights are kind of cool -- the case has a starburst-like pattern of lights that serves as the operation indicator. The lights fade in and out when the drive is operating. A bit more interesting than the usual single LED-type indicator.

Very pleased, and hope it will be as reliable as my other external Seagate. But, in case it's not, there's a five year warranty from Seagate.

Highly recommend!
text_fidelity_b: Seagate FreeAgent Go 320 GB USB 2.0 Portable External Hard Drive ST903203FAA2E1-RK (Black)

AKG (A Samsung Brand) N700NC M2 Over-Ear Foldable Wireless , Active Noise Cancelling Headphones - Black (US Version), 2.6, Model:GP-N700HAHCIWA Ok I can be a bit of a headphone snob, but at a near $300 price point I have some pretty high expectations. I ran them through my standard audio tests and these passed every one with flying colors. Bottomline, where most wireless sets fail is with bass, either its lacking or they overcompensate for it at the expense of everything else. (I'm talking to you SkullCandy). These however managed to be astounding on bass without it being overwhelming. Deep rich sounds, but mid and upper still came in crystal clear. It was impressive.

They also manage to have noise canceling without the annoying hiss present in the high end SkullCandy set I recently reviewed. The AKG's are superior and even performed better than my beloved, but admittedly old Sennheisers. How they would match up against a newer pair I can't say though, I will fangirl all day over a high end set of Senn's, but these AKGs give them some serious competition.

The ambient pass-through was a welcome addition, and these paired effortlessly via blue tooth. The ear cups were comfortable, although warm like every other pair of closed noise-canceling headsets I've tried. I will be honest I tend to prefer an open headset, but that is more preference than anything to do with this set. The ear cups were smaller than other pairs I've worn, I'm petite so that wasn't an issue but if you got yourself some good sized ears keep that in mind.

So if you have $300 burning a hole in your pocket and need some very well balanced wireless headphones, I highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: AKG (A Samsung Brand) N700NC M2 Over-Ear Foldable Wireless , Active Noise Cancelling Headphones - Black (US Version), 2.6, Model:GP-N700HAHCIWA

MIATONE Outdoor Waterproof Portable Bluetooth Speaker Wireless - Green When I first opened the box, I kind of doubted that this compact bluetooth speaker was worth $50. But, after I got it fully charged (which didn't take long) and connected to my phone (super easy), I opened my graphic equalizer app and then started my favorite Pandora station. I cannot say enough about how surprised and pleased I am about the sound quality! The bass is thumping! The treble is crisp and clear! I have other BT speakers this size and none of them even come close to the quality! This Miatone TWS BT speaker is awesome!

Note: because the sound comes out both sides and both ends, you need to keep the control panel at the top (or the bottom). Otherwise, you lose some of the sound quality. So, propping it up in the right position is essential to getting the best quality sound.

I had to knock off one star on the portability factor for one thing; it's a perfect cylinder with no flat edge to keep it from rolling away. And, placing it on end will muffle part of the bass, as both ends have that wonderful bass speaker in them. I guess you can make sure that you place it either on a perfectly flat surface or if it's on a slope, that the included cord is underneath like a 'wheel chock'. But, overall, that's just a minor oversight. I still have to give this amazing little BOOMBOX five stars, because of the quality of construction and the amazing sound. I have JBL's this size that don't sound as good. Super happy with this purchase. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: MIATONE Outdoor Waterproof Portable Bluetooth Speaker Wireless - Green

text_fidelity_a:
Yamaha AVENTAGE RX-A880 7.2-ch 4K Ultra HD AV Receiver with HDR Dolby Vision Dolby Atmos Wi-Fi Phono YPAO and MusicCast. Works with Alexa. Update: I really love this machine. You give a lot of things five stars if they're really good products, but this one deserves bonus. I've been slowly going through the full 200+ page manual to make sure I don't miss any features and to get the most out of this thing, and I'm continually thrilled. Also, I give a lot of things controlled by apps low ratings because I tend to hate screwing around with my phone, but in this case, the Yamaha AV controller app only adds to the value, with the best part being you don't NEED it to take advantage of all the receiver's functionality, but it's a joy to have sometimes to make fine adjustments without having to turn on the TV. I really like it for adjusting net radio stations and stuff like that or fine tuning music sounds - again, without having to turn on the TV. This also makes up for the one negative I mentioned below about not being able to change all the settings from a web page. Great stuff!

Original review:

Before this, I had two Sony receivers in my living room. My secondary is a much older model - about 12 or so years old - that does not have HDMI and I use it for my whole house audio system. My primary is (was - it just got replaced) a 3-5 year old Sony model that is admittedly in a lower class than this Yamaha receiver (the secondary was in a higher class in its time, I think).

While I usually have all Sony stuff, I was completely willing to try another well-known Japanese brand who specializes in receivers and amps. And - it's just awesome. Totally. Not a single regret about the switch. The RX-A880 gave me back everything I lost going from my older, higher-end Sony to my newer one, AND it gave me so many nice surprises on the way! As anyone can tell you that it sounds good and looks good, I'll concentrate on this little details that I discovered during setup:

1) Besides the seven HDMI inputs, it also has a composite video, a component video, two optical audio, one extra (second belongs to component) coax audio, and two composite audio inputs, not to mention phono.

The great thing is that you can assign different audio inputs to any of the video inputs. So, for example, I decided to keep my Wii around since I now have a component input (and it takes up almost no space), but the cable is component video with composite audio, but the component video input on this has coax for the audio. Bummer. But no, you can change it. Example number two is I have a computer in my telecom closet hooked up to this with both HDMI and line-out audio. For circumstances too complicated to define here, audio does not output via the HDMI. But because of this feature, I can make the audio appear when I select the HDMI input OR when I just want to listen to the audio directly (with no HDMI output). Perfect.

2) 9 Speaker outputs. First, I'm so happy to have the 2-zone thing back (my secondary receiver has it, but my other, newer Sony did not - it only had A/B speakers that shared an amp). But this one you can actually have 7.1 AND a second zone (although you can't play them at the same time. This is really cool if you want the best of both worlds. I don't know if I can find a place for two more speakers in my setup, but ...it's nice to have the option. Supposedly, this all works automatically. I imagine it could work fine, but I am unable to try it at the moment.

3) 2-zone done better. My older Sony had 2-zone, but the controls were - frankly - atrocious. It was always confusing, even for someone like me who can be a super A/V nerd and memorize anything. The way I use it now is just to keep the remote on Zone-2, and do Zone-1 on the unit itself.

This Yamaha, however, has a simple switch on the remote, and you're either controlling one zone or the other depending on that switch. Simple and effective. You can also control it from the unit, unlike the older Sony.

4) 8 custom presets, all controlled directly from the remote. Another 8 for Zone 2?!

The one complaint I read by a reviewer was that you have to scroll through all the inputs from the remote to get to what you want. But that doesn't matter for two reasons: first, you can change the settings to skip anything you don't want. But, second, with 8 custom presets - and each with their own remote button - you probably don't even ever need to scroll through the inputs anyway.

And the custom presets are great. You can turn on and off a bunch of features like whether or not it changes your HDMI out settings, if it uses your YPAO settings, extra bass, which speakers it uses, etc. And it even can link the second zone!

Two great examples:

I can't stand to watch regular background TV with the surround sound on because it makes the commercials that much more obnoxious. But of course I like big booming bass and surround for movies. And it's also annoying to switch the unit off and on all the time, especially if you want to use control for HDMI. So I have one preset for very flat TV sound using just the front speakers that is clearer than-, but no more annoying than-, my regular TV speakers. Then I have another preset for surround sound and big bass for movie watching.

I have one preset for straight music just in zone 1. Then I have another preset for straight music in both zones one and two. It turns on zone 2 automatically. I could not figure out how to make a preset just for zone 2, but it seems that when I am controlling zone 2 on the remote, I can make 8 more presets just for zone 2. You can not adjust these presets via menu, from what I can tell, though.

5) 14 character names on the front of the unit in dot matrix. My other receivers were all limited to 8 characters. You can see all 14 at once, which is great.

6) Much more robust networking. I haven't played with this too awful much yet, but it seems that if you start listening to a playlist or an album on your NAS, then the next time you go back to "server", it will start playing where you left off (well, the song you left off at will start over again, instead of at the exact moment you left at), but at least this way you don't have to turn the TV on just to play some music. I suppose you could create a playlist of all Death Metal, and then you just have a stream going whenever you want it. It also seems like you can actually sign into Pandora and all the other stations and listen to your own account. And all the Internet/Network stuff is a separate scroll-through than the other inputs. I really like how that is set up.

6) The "program up/down" buttons on the remote can be programmed to do about 10 different things. I picked to have the dialogue increased or decreased for when you can't hear what people are saying even though everything else is loud enough. To be clear, I think this depends on if the dialogue is known to the decoder. I haven't tried all the other options yet.

7) Remote is awesome. Besides what I mentioned above, you can also make some changes to the red/green/yellow/blue buttons, but I wish you could really program those completely to your liking. Everything is laid out nicely, and the second zone even makes sense, as I mentioned above.

8) I realize the second HDMI output would be great if you also have a projector or something like that. With it, you can have access to all your devices without having to rewire anything. Haven't used it yet, but am glad to have the extra functionality.

...

There's plenty more, but I'm forgetting some of the details right now. I've only played with this thing for a few days, but I like it more and more. The one thing that is missing is that you can't change all the options via the webpage. You can change some, but I liked with my newer Sony the fact that I could look at and change all my custom presets without having to turn the TV and go through all that. I'm only comparing this to my two Sony units so you get my frame of reference, but realize this Yamaha model is in a higher class than those. Regardless, I love this thing, and it has a lot of great functionality and no serious drawbacks that I've noticed yet. Recommended (obviously).

text_fidelity_a:
Bluetooth Earbuds,Kurdene Wireless Earbuds with Wireless Charging case,Touch Control in Ear Bluetooth 5.0 Waterproof Headphones CVC 8.0 Noise Cancelling Earphones with Deep Bass Sound for Sports(Pink) Pros

1. Excellent sound, with more clarity than the other Bluetooth earbuds I own. They are especially better for listening to music.

2. The earbuds and their case have a sleek, attractive design.

Cons

1. Each small ear piece operates separately. They are not attached to each other via a plastic-coated wire as is typically the case for earbuds. This means that, when I remove these earbuds from my ears, because there is no wire holding them securely around my neck, they must be carefully and consistently placed in their carrying case, and then either set in a safe, easily remembered location, or placed in my pants pocket. Neither option is desirable. It is extremely difficult to not get distracted and set down these earbuds in a random location, such that afterwards I have to waste a lot of time looking for them. And the problem with slipping them into a pocket is that there is a strong possibility I might accidentally leave them there, such that they end up in the washer and dryer and are ruined. In short, the risk of losing or destroying these earbuds is enormous!

2. Each ear piece must be turned ON/OFF separately, one after the other. This is a hassle.

3. The ON/OFF controls are extremely difficult to engage. You touch an ear piece and hold it for several seconds to turn each ear piece on or off. There is no button. The ear piece is somehow sensing the pressure of the touch of a fingertip. I frequently have great difficulty locating and pressing the exact spot required in order to turn these earbuds on or off. This is a major pain!

4. Volume is controlled the same way as the ON/OFF function, by magically managing to touch the earpiece in the exact, necessary location with the appropriate amount of fingertip pressure. It is very difficult to accomplish that, and the frustration of failing at this onerous task again and again is maddening!

For all of the above reasons, I wouldn’t recommend these earbuds to my worst enemy!
text_fidelity_b: Bluetooth Earbuds,Kurdene Wireless Earbuds with Wireless Charging case,Touch Control in Ear Bluetooth 5.0 Waterproof Headphones CVC 8.0 Noise Cancelling Earphones with Deep Bass Sound for Sports(Pink)

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech HD Pro Webcam C920, Widescreen Video Calling and Recording, 1080p Camera, Desktop or Laptop Webcam (Discontinued by manufacturer) I was able to do a direct side-by-side comparison between three Logitech webcams: the C920, C615, and C525. Here is what I found:

Right away I noticed that the C920 was a superior product - as it should be, considering it is Logitech's flagship webcam at the moment. But my initial impression was that the extra features might not be worth the size and setup tradeoff. There are three things that the C920 does not have:

1) While all three models attach to your computer monitor in about the same way and all three can tilt up and down, only the C525 and C615 can turn side to side. In fact, they can turn around 360 degrees and more. The C920, however, has a threaded tripod mount, as does the C615.

2) The C920 lacks the excellent "fold-and-go" design of the other two models, which makes packing and travelling easy, while protecting the lenses. In contrast, the C920 is much larger and stationary.

3) The C615 comes with a shorter USB cable AND an extension for more versatility. The C920 - like the C525 - comes with only a full length cable (~6'). My wish for all three models is that they come with a detachable USB cable, which would make them all much more portable and easy to carry around, especially in this age when most people travel with at least one or two USB cables.

But when I actually sat down to do some serious comparisons, I realized just how much more advanced the C920 is, most notably in its use of H.264 compression and its autofocus feature.

H.264 is a standard being utilized more and more for video of all sorts, and it makes a huge difference here. Having used all three webcams on the same computer and with the same software, the C920 compresses 1080p video completely while recording and takes about 49MB per 1 minute of recording on the highest settings (720p for one minute takes about 31MB). That uses *.mp4 format.

Meanwhile, the C615 and C525 use *.wmv format and take 99MB and 44MB for one minute of video at 1080p and 720p, respectively. The real problem, though, is that you then have to sit and wait for the video to compress if you are working in 1080.

If you're interested, The C920 has 1 zoom level at 1080 and 4 levels at 720. The C615 has 0 zoom levels at 1080 and about 10 at 720. The C525 has about 10 at 720. All can be used during recording, but the quality involved with the C920 is again far superior.

Also, the autofocus is much better on the C920, with less flickering and light change. You can really get up close and show off your pores and beard growth.

In conclusion, the optics and hardware of the C920 are obviously superior to the others, which are already high quality. If I am using the webcam while highly mobile, then I may opt for one of the others - I might even just settle for the C525 because it's a tiny bit smaller than the C615 and I believe you cannot use the C615 to make 1080p video calling, even if your hotel's Internet service could keep up with the data rate. However, if I am using a webcam at a stationary computer, or am really a videophile, then I definitely want the bigger workhorse.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech HD Pro Webcam C920, Widescreen Video Calling and Recording, 1080p Camera, Desktop or Laptop Webcam (Discontinued by manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
SAMSUNG 23.5” CF396 Curved Computer Monitor, AMD FreeSync for Advanced Gaming, 4ms Response Time, Wide Viewing Angle, Ultra Slim Design, LC24F396FHNXZA, Black Now, in all fairness, I probably just spoiled myself rotten when I bought a $5000.00 Eizo professional monitor 8 or 10 years ago. Prior to that I'd been using two much less-expensive Samsung monitors and had been perfectly happy with them (excepting their longevity - neither of them lasted more than two or three years before going completely dead). Then, as I was embarking on a career as a pro photographer, I decided I needed a professional-quality monitor with precise and consistent color reproduction, so after hemming and hawing over the price for a while, I bit the proverbial bullet and laid down the cash for a new Eizo ColorEdge CG276. And honestly, at that time, I noticed that what I saw on my screen looked very nice, but I don't recall it blowing my mind - proof that the way to *really* appreciate what you've got is to do without it. Because I've now tried replacing this Eizo monitor (which is still working perfectly in every respect and which I'm still using and writing this review on now) with less expensive monitors twice, and each time I've shaken my head in disbelief that anybody could use a monitor with such crappy resolution and image quality, let alone think it was good.

That, sadly, but I guess as is to be expected, was my experience with this Samsung.

It didn't matter that the screen was curved; what I saw on the screen looked so terrible that it wouldn't matter if the monitor was a freaking planetarium, or a perfect globe surrounding me on all sides while I floated in the center via...I don't know...jetpack or something. I'd just have that much more poorly rendered graphics to look at.

I've attached five photos: one of the progress bar as it appears on my Eizo monitor, and two as it appears on this Samsung, followed by one of the Apple logo as it appears on the Eizo and finally, the Apple logo as it appears on the Samsung. You be the judge. (UPDATE: I just noticed that Amazon's website doesn't display the images in the same order in which you upload them (or at least it isn't with my images)...so suffice it to say that the really smooth and nice-looking progress bar and text and Apple logo are the Eizo's screen, and the really jaggy, glary, awful-looking ones are the Samsung's.)

I don't have the technical understanding of monitors required to explain which monitor-related variable it is, exactly, that makes the image quality on this Samsung so unsatisfactory (resolution? pixel size/shape? dunno.), but something definitely does it.

Maybe once you've used an Eizo on a Mac, you can never go back. So be it. If I really need a new monitor I'll just save my pennies until I can afford another Eizo...or at least something with much better specs than this Samsung. Because boy, was it a disappointment.

Ah well...lesson learned (kinda...even though I don't really know *why* I thought the Samsung sucked). I've boxed it back up and arranged my hassle-free return through Amazon and will at least get my money back...the return policy and process being two reasons I buy through Amazon in the first place. And I'll simply content myself to go on using a top-quality flat screen (that I can smoothly and easily raise and lower and pivot and even turn from landscape to portrait and back!) instead of trying to swap it out for a vastly inferior curved one (that I can only tilt up and down).
text_fidelity_b: SAMSUNG 23.5” CF396 Curved Computer Monitor, AMD FreeSync for Advanced Gaming, 4ms Response Time, Wide Viewing Angle, Ultra Slim Design, LC24F396FHNXZA, Black

Amazon Basics Adjustable Tablet/iPad Mount Holder for Microphone and Music Stand, Black So when I ordered this mount, it was based on the title description and one small photo. Here's what I've learned since.

It's meant to be mounted to a post like what might be a part of a monitor stand. So the clamp is the shape of a hook. It does not clamp well onto flat surfaces. I wanted to mount this onto a shelf board, so I've got a plastic tube inserted on the hook side to occupy space to help it sit flat.

The holders are not spring loaded. Each end is tighten by a knob. The knobs can be difficult to access depending on the orientation of the arm. In my case one of the knob was right up against the arm. So you don't just walk up and slide you tablet into this, it needs to be set up.

The rounded retainers are plastic, not rubber. So you can't just have them on both sides. The have to be on the top or bottom or in opposing corners.

As a tablet it holder, it works. But there are far more user friendly designs out there.

I hope you found this review a little bit helpful. Thank you for reading.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Basics Adjustable Tablet/iPad Mount Holder for Microphone and Music Stand, Black

ProElife Ultra Thin Silicone Full Size Keyboard Cover Skin for 2017 2018 Apple iMac Magic Keyboard with Numeric Keypad MQ052LL/A A1843 US Layout (Item Folded in Packaging) (Ombre Blue) UPDATE (12/25/2021):

I have removed this skin (bought on January 27, 2020) for 3 reasons.
1. The keys were not so visible below the skin because it has become more translucent instead of remaining transparent.
2. The shift key on the left side was ripped from being used and from my fingernail, I would think. IOW, it's not so tough.
3. A sticky liquid has formed between my keyboard and the skin. I removed it with more than just wiping. No solvent has been used at any time. Perhaps the silicone reacted with the plastic keys. Nothing has ever been spilled on the keyboard. Still, I have a skin on the keyboard as protection against any liquid OR dust OR hair getting into my keyboard that I have been using since 2008 when it was new.

My replacement (Allinside) is now in place and I can once again see the keys.
The skin fits the keys such that it does NOT have to wrap around the edges of the keyboard.

UPDATE (7/14/2018): After one year I have to replace this keyboard skin because it is wearing out in several places, mainly the left side command key where there is a ¼ inch slit. When I have to type a long document / letter, I remove the skin so I can type faster on the aluminum keyboard because the keys require only a light touch. I have not switched to a BT keyboard because this one is so good, and the fact that it is wired is not a problem with a little tape to keep the cable out of the way when I slide the keyboard shelf in and out. The skin I received is transparent with nothing printed on any of the keys.

For those who have the wired Apple aluminum extended keyboard (with keypad), this product fits correctly to protect the keyboard from dust and spills. It is in use on my Mac Pro (early 2008). The description says for iMac, but it fits any of these keyboards of this style, not just the iMac keyboard.

It arrives folded, but that does not matter if it comes from a seller in the US who delivers it in a timely manner.

The keyboard cover does make it necessary to slow down the typing speed. That's not a real problem unless one is a touch typist or writer who spends a lot of time on the keyboard.

Telescopes for Adults Astronomy, 70mm Aperture 400mm AZ Mount Astronomical Telescope for Astronomy Beginners Kids Adults - Carry Bag Upgraded Tripod and Phone Holder for Photography The telescope's purpose is to bird watch/identify visitors to the old-growth forest/marsh preserve adjoining our lot. I plan to keep the telescope 'permanent' through the second-story game room windows. We have a spectacular shot through the preserve. We live on a major migratory flyway. North American bird migrations and including the swarm of Monarch butterflies pass by the windows.

As to astronomical use, the refractor magnification lens system is entry-level. This general refractor-grade telescope serves as the smaller spotting scope on larger reflector telescopes. The scope has standard interfaces to mount better glass and wider angle lenses. It's a great basic platform to expand with higher quality and wider FOV lenses. I have plans to mount a made for purpose high res electronic magnification CCD to capture images. I've already replaced the tripod with a more robust design.

I'm delighted with the telescope as a basic platform for customizing. The main attraction is standard lens interfaces and scalability. The optical enhancements get pricey and will quickly exceed the purchase price.

Easy to assemble, easy to use. A beginner will get the hang of viewing with a little use with progressively smaller apertures as magnification is increased. There are viewing techniques available on YouTubes to investigate.

As expected and fully comparable to other refractor telescopes with a 70mm objective lens and 400mm focal length. Nice value for money.
text_fidelity_b: Telescopes for Adults Astronomy, 70mm Aperture 400mm AZ Mount Astronomical Telescope for Astronomy Beginners Kids Adults - Carry Bag Upgraded Tripod and Phone Holder for Photography

It provides a significant upgrade on the pseudo-4k projector with an impressive 2600 lumens making it one of the brightest projectors out there easily surpassing the 1500 lumens you would get with the entry level Sony true 4K projector. One of the big upgrades is the move to 18Gbps bandwidth giving you the ability to do 4K at 60Hz. Note that you do need to have a wired connection to get the full 18Gbps -- you only get 12 if you do the wireless option that the 5050ube offers over the regular 5050ub. Even with the reduced bandwidth that you get with the wireless setup, it is a great convenience to have the ability to stream from sources without having to run a wire from the source to the actual projector.

Another great aspect of the 5050 is the motorized lens which is a feature that other more expensive true-4k projectors do not offer. Of course with Epson you do get exceptional HDR quality as well as amazing black.

This is an impressive pseudo-4K projector that provides features that are not even found in some entry level true 4K projectors. If you are not absolutely dying to get true 4k, then this should be one of the projectors you should consider.

It offers a lot of functionality in a compact size: a flashlight, AM radio, FM radio and weather band radio. It runs off of an internal rechargeable battery that is kept charged either via solar power, USB connection or by cranking the handle. It can also serve as a source to charge a cell phone (albeit with very limited capacity to do so since the internal battery is only rated at 800mAh).

It works pretty well. The flashlight is very bright - had no problems lighting my way down a dark stairway and in a totally dark room. The radio is OK. The reception is spotty and it only picked up a few of the very strong stations in the area. It's very susceptible to positioning - moving it just a couple of inches turned a clear station into static.

Cranking the handle to keep it charged is pretty easy. It turns easily and the handle is comfortable. According to the manual, one minute of cranking equals 30 minutes of flashlight use or 20 minutes of radio use.

This is a good product to keep on hand in case of emergency, such as a bad storm or extended power outage. It won't keep you cool in the summer or warm in the winter, but at least you can see where you're going and listen to the radio. Definitely worth a spot in the emergency kit. The only shortcoming is the somewhat limited radio reception.

text_fidelity_a:
Inateck 3.5 Hard Drive Enclosure, Aluminum USB 3.0 Sata HDD Enclosure, FE3001 I've had this enclosure for almost 2 years. My five year old computer was very slow and I was having lots of trouble with it and the enclosure connecting to it. I did get it to connect and do one backup, but that was it. So, I thought surely it was my pc that was the problem. It would either not connect or it would not do anything...like I didn't have it plugged in. I just thought all three connections had to be made properly for it to come on and do it's job. I am not completely tech stupid, nor savvy.
I am disabled, so I was saving for a new computer. I have had lots of sickness over this time, and getting to this was not a huge priority and I never came back to read reviews. I wish I had.
I finally did recently get a new pc, and just the other day wanted to give it another go. When I plugged it in, again, there seemed to be no power... and then suddenly there was a burning smell and smoke coming from the enclosure where the power supply went in. It was quite scary, because I almost did not catch it soon enough.
I took a long shot and contacted the company anyways, even though it had been such a while to explain the long ordeal, and why I had not contacted sooner... Among my sickness, I was giving the device the benefit of the doubt, because I honestly thought it was my pc.
This is the message I received in return "In this case, it is highly commended to stop using this hard drive enclosure.
According to your information, this item is faulty. Regarding our products, a 12-month warranty is provided, however, it is obviously that the item ordered on 2016 has been far beyond its warranty. Hope that you could understand."
They did offer a 15% "return after purchase" discount refund if I would purchase a new one. But, as I am disabled, I cannot afford to do that at this time.
Hopefully, my backup really is on the hard drive that this unit supposedly saved it to that one time, as some beloved photos of my deceased father are on there, and I don't have them anywhere else.
I wish I were more tech savvy and didn't stay sick so much... Even so, I wouldn't have known the problem until I got a new pc anyways. Based on my experience and other reviews, I would not recommend this enclosure to anyone.
I do hope this helps someone.
text_fidelity_b: Inateck 3.5 Hard Drive Enclosure, Aluminum USB 3.0 Sata HDD Enclosure, FE3001

Sony XBR-65A8G 65 Inch TV: BRAVIA OLED 4K Ultra HD Smart TV with HDR and Alexa Compatibility - 2019 Model Overall, I really love this TV. The picture is great. Our last HD TV was good but sometimes it showed all the imperfections. I mean, you could see the makeup on the actors faces. Takes away from the realism. This one has the sharpness without the byproducts? Not sure how to say it.

Setting this up was interesting. It comes in a box that is actually very easy to remove it from. The screen is huge and very thin. I was afraid we were going to break it. It is very light for it's size, basically the same weight as our old 47" LG flatscreen. We ended up putting it on the stand instead of on the wall mount because it would have been difficult to fit due to the alcove only being about 2 inches wider than the screen. It does seem fairly sturdy on the stand. We laid it flat on the cardboard while attaching the stand. The directions tell you to hold it up while screwing it in, but that seemed a little stupid to me without a few people to hold it. You do need to let it hang at the edge of the table or whatever if you are going to do it that way.

Setting it up with my phone didn't work as easily as they made it seem. I ended up inputting the wifi password and going that way instead of taking the settings from my phone after it sat in the checking mode for a while. It also only seems to have 3 HDMI connections which might not be enough, depending on how many "toys" you have. I was kind of surprise there wasn't more. And maybe there was one more than we didn't understand whether it was usable?

We have Directv, so we have to have a separate controller for that. There is an IR attachment that can be set up to allow you to use the TV remote for both, but it was kind of complicated and once the TV was setup it is too big to go back and move it to check for these things. This may be the biggest problem for us with the TV. As you can see in the picture, it is a tight fit. It is also huge. (good for viewing, not good for moving) So once it is set up, that is it. If you don't attach it to the wall (it doesn't come with the wall hanger) you may want to get some kind of tip protection, especially if you have kids. The screen will break if it falls over based on how thin it is, which would be dangerous.

I received this item free in exchange for my honest opinion. Honestly, if I hadn't gotten it free, I would personally not have bought it because I am not that particular about the TV, even if I appreciate the great picture. However, my husband probably would have as he watches a lot of movies and this is something he has been eyeing for a while, waiting for the prices to come down a bit more.

The only quibble I have is that it lacks an on/off switch. Not a big deal, but having a switch can come in handy at times.

ArmorSuit MilitaryShield Screen Protector for Apple iPad Mini 1/2/3 - [Max Coverage] Anti-Bubble HD Clear Film I really can't say enough good things about this, especially at the price I paid on Amazon.

I'm VERY very very OCD about my screen protectors, and the unique wet application of this one makes it an absolute joy to apply and to use.

The instructions are very easy to follow, all you need is in the kit.

So you spray the spray stuff on, slide the shield around until it's where you want it, then squeegee it down and let it sit. For me, the iPad was completely useable immediately.

What's even better is, a few months later, the corners were lifting and getting some grit under them (not a flaw in the shield ... I was using this with an iPad cover whose silicone covers move a little and shove the shield up). I pulled the corners up, sprayed the solution on (they send way more than you need for one application), flicked off the grit, squeegeed it back down ... good as new!

Given the flexible nature of the film I think a lot of devices that get a lot of rubbing at the edges might get this peeling effect, but it's great how keeping that bottle of spray around lets you fix it right up. When I peeled the corner back i accidentally touched some tissue to the guard, and it stuck to it, and I thought I was done for ... but spraying the liquid solution on, the tissue let go and like I said, it went back down at the corners as good as new.

I'll absolutely be buying these for all future big electronic purchases.
text_fidelity_b: ArmorSuit MilitaryShield Screen Protector for Apple iPad Mini 1/2/3 - [Max Coverage] Anti-Bubble HD Clear Film

text_fidelity_a:
Logitech Harmony 700 Rechargeable Remote with Color Screen (Black) [Discontinued by Manufacturer] Solid remote with major flaws. Yes, the battery does last a long time...no issue there. But there is no battery life indicator on the screen and you don't get any warning when running low. So unless you plug it in regularly (which defeats the purpose of long battery life) you go from working perfectly to dead with no warning. While plugged in a battery graphic with a bolt tells you it's charging, but doesn't tell you the % charged or when it is done. When you unplug it the battery graphic doesn't go away, and it doesn't return to normal operation. You can push all the buttons you want, the battery graphic stays on the screen and it doesn't work. The only way to get it working is to take out the batteries and put them back in. And after you do that, you have to go through the tutorial before you can start using it again (thankfully, it does retain the device programming). What a hassle.

And when is Harmony going to get rid of the remote assistant? Like previous models, it constantly asks you if you want to hide the assistant, and it won't operate until you answer. Does the assistant even do anything the help button doesn't? If Harmony is so in love with this outdated 1990s feature, just put an assistant button on the remote and keep the damn thing hidden unless WE decide to turn it on. And the ability to skip the tutorial would be nice too. Nobody wants to be constantly answering to their remote.

Harmony is very good at making initial programming of the remote easy, but seem to give up on the interface after that. Once I'm done programming it, I don't want to mess with it any more, and I CERTAINLY don't want it to interrupt operation. Do what I ask you to do, otherwise sit there and look pretty.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech Harmony 700 Rechargeable Remote with Color Screen (Black) [Discontinued by Manufacturer]

text_fidelity_a:
Coby Kyros 7-Inch Android 2.3 4 GB Internet Touchscreen Tablet - MID7012-4G (Black) I never owned a tablet or a smartphone so I suppose if I did my review might be different but I think this is a pretty neat little tablet and the price is pretty great too.

I've had it for a couple of days and downloaded the Amazon App store which has most of the apps anyone could need. I mean seriously how many apps does an average person really use? I have downloaded quite a few games for both myself and my kids, the Kindle app, I heart Radio app, and the US newspaper app. So far its holding all of it but I also ordered a microsdhc card for extra space to hold more apps and e-books. I have a regular Kindle that I've had for quite a few years and I am able to transfer most of the books onto this tablet also (I haven't tried downloading all of them since my son uses a few for school). It has where you can calibrate the stylus. Also if you longpress the stylus onto the wallpaper it will let you change the wallpaper in the background.

It does not come with a camera and flashplayer is not installed (but what I understand you can install a "lite" version of flashplayer which I have not done as of yet). The touchscreen is more geared toward using the stylus (which is included) which is a let down to some people. You can use your fingertip but it isn't as responsive as with the stylus IMO. It also comes with a sleeve (that has a place for your stylus) and earphones. There is a charger and a USB cable. There is another cable which I'm not sure exactly what its for (sorry). I haven't used the other cables just yet (except the charger of course). As for battery life it does seem like it runs down pretty quickly (perhaps 3-4 hours). Of course, that may change depending on the type of apps you have running. I know a lot of people worry about reading books from this rather than the Kindle type e-ink. I, personally, like reading at night before I go to sleep and with the Kindle I had to keep a lamp on just to see the page..(barely)...whereas this isn't like that (my eyes are much happier!) You can change the brightness of the screen if you are worried about the brightness bothering your eyes.

I have my email accessible to the Coby Kyros so I can check it throughout the day since my daughter takes off with my laptop quite often. I also downloaded the Dolphin mini browser which I like better than the browser sent with the Kyros. It comes with the GetJar app store which has quite a few apps but Amazon has more.

Of course, I cannot guarantee how well it will hold up because I've only had it for a couple of days but overall its a nice simple little tablet. I've seen the reviews of more expensive tablets and I don't want to spend $400 on a tablet that's rated two stars. I was willing to take the chance and so far I'm happy with my purchase. I rated it 4 stars because the speaker is kinda crappy...I haven't tried listening to the radio with earphones...hopefully it sounds better. And also I wish that it was easier to install flash (I've been looking on the internet but it seems like you have to be really a techie to do it...and I'm not!) It's not an Ipad (or Ipod) so you can't rate this tablet against a product like that (of course it's half the price of a Ipod touch).
text_fidelity_b: Coby Kyros 7-Inch Android 2.3 4 GB Internet Touchscreen Tablet - MID7012-4G (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Pixel Mago Canon Speedlite ETTL High Speed 5D2 5D3 6D 7D 60D External Speedlite While this flash doesn’t outperform the Canon Speedlite, it comes the closest of any of the Speedlite “clones” I’ve tried so far, and does so with impressive build quality.

I was impressed with this right out of the box mainly due to the care taken with packaging. No, packaging doesn’t impact the performance of the flash, but it does take the worry out of getting one that is damaged due to UPS handling. The flash is packed in a carry case (which is very well-made and has cushioning) and, in turn, packed inside of an air-filled tube case. Together they provide more than ample protection against transit-born bruises short of being run over by the UPS truck.

The flash feels very solid. The head articulates up/down/left/right and has indents at the most commonly used angles. The head is a bit stiff to move, but I consider that as a positive since I don’t want the head getting bumped out of place when I have it positioned the way I want it.

The hotshoe frame is plastic but feels very solid. There’s a rotating locking ring to keep it in place while on the camera. It made contact and worked just fine on a 5D Mark II, a 4D and a Rebel.

The battery compartment door has a spring-loaded hinge so it pops up when unlatched. Again, good build quality on that (which is a common point of failure on other low-cost flashes I’ve used). It uses 4 AA batteries. It ran fine on rechargeables.

The control panel and LCD screen are both easy to use and see for the most part. The buttons beep when pressed, but that can be turned off if you want a silent operation. Some of the icons on the screen are very small – I needed to squint a bit to make some of them out. Then again, my aging eyes could be a contributing factor.

Most of the commands are executed by pressing a button and then selecting options using a rotating wheel. The wheel is the only part that didn’t work all that well at times. Sometimes a single twist moved it through the menu; other times I needed to twist it a couple of times to get it to register.

The capabilities of this flash are very impressive given the price point. It offers synch flash, manual flash, curtain synch, up to 1/8000 second synch, master/slave mode, AF assist beam, TTL flash, zoom settings and an LED lamp. It also has a nice amount of convenience features such as auto off (with various timed settings ranging from 5 minutes to 2 hours), a lock mode, screen on/off and test mode. It even has a USB port that can be used to update the firmware should updates be available (at this writing I am not aware of any updates).

The manual is not great. It offers a decent listing of the capabilities, but is often sparse in pointing out the details. But, if you have some measure of experience with a flash, it’s not hard to figure out (with a bit of experimenting) how to use it.

Given the price, this is an excellent value. It probably won’t suit the needs of a professional photographer but for an amateur (even a very avid one) it’s an excellent alternative to Canon gear at a much nicer price.
text_fidelity_b: Pixel Mago Canon Speedlite ETTL High Speed 5D2 5D3 6D 7D 60D External Speedlite

text_fidelity_a:
AGPtEK 16GB Portable MP3 Player(Expandable Up to 128GB), Music Player/Voice Recorder/FM Radio with HD Headphone and Adjustable Sport Armband, M28, Black Software Features:
This AGPtEK mp3 player is a really good alternative to an ipod or zune which is more expensive and offers less storage space while offering the opportunity to drag and drop files into the mp3 player folder directly, once it's connected via usb cable to your computer. This feature is important to me, because not all my music is properly tagged, so music organizing software like itunes doesn't recognise the files. This is no problem with the AGPtEK mp3 player, since I can always manually find the file and drop it in.
Hardware Features: The build is attractive and sturdy. I appreciate the glass display and nice solid but light aluminum casing. The shape is a basic rectangle which works fine for me since I like a minimalist look. One thing I don't like about the build is that the click wheel click very loudly and is a little stiff, which is a hassle to use when you're trying to scroll down your music list.The wheel feels a little cheap, its quality is not on par with the rest of the build. The screen is not as large as a typical ipod's but is sufficient. The title of your song will have to scroll a bit to be read fully, which can be kind annoying. ANother great thing is that you can upgrade storage using a micro SD chip which means you're quadrupling your storage. score!

Music Playback features: They have a nice EQ option if you're into that. The fast forward is really slow. The mp3 player plays a bunch of different formats like mp3, oog, wav, flac, etc... You can also store audiobooks, videos, photos, and record sound. I havn't use these features yet.

Accessories: The arm band is a nice bonus. It fits perfectly and leaves holes for charging and headphones. It holds the mp3 player snuggly. The band is smooth and not scratchy. If you have small arms the band can be pretty big, it's adjustable but there will be somg extra band hanging around. t is fastened by velcro.
The headphones are like $10 quality. They're not bad, but they're not audiophile. They don't fit very well as I have small ears but they'll do in a pinch.

Charging: There is an option to charge and transfer or charge and play music once you connect the player to your computer. CHarging it fully takes about 1-2 hours. The mp3's battery is very good, I haven't been able to drain the battery completely, but keeping it off, it's been able to stay charged for over 3 days.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony WI-XB400 Wireless In-Ear Extra Bass Headset/Headphones with mic for phone call, Black PROS

1. This product is made by Sony which, in my experience, consistently manufactures products of the highest professional standard—and this product is no exception.
2. These earbuds have excellent sound, definitely better than a comparable but cheaper alternative that I had been using just prior to purchasing this product. As advertised, the bass is of much higher quality than for any other earbuds I’ve owned.
3. The quality of the packaging and the manuals for this product far exceeds the quality of most similar products, especially those that are from small Chinese companies.
4. This product uses a USB-C charging cable, rather than micro USB like all of the other Bluetooth earbud sets I have owned. That’s very convenient, because I have a USB-C charging cable in every room of my house for charging my phone.
5. The ON/OFF and volume switches are sturdy and easy to locate by touch.

CONS

1. The cable that goes around your neck is very flexible, unlike the other earbud set I have of this type. It would have been useful to have it be more firm so that it stays in place around my neck instead of sliding off when I bend over.
2. I got these earbuds on sale at a significant discount. At full, retail price, these earbuds cost double the amount of a similar type of earbuds which are not quite up to the Sony standard. For that reason, at full price, I would have to think hard about whether I can afford this brand on a fixed income.

Cons:

Accsoon CineEye Video Transmitter, 5G Wireless Live Transmission to 4 Devices, 1080p WiFi HDMI, 100 Meter Range, Supports Android & iOS, RGB, 3D LUT Loading, Incredibly Low Latency – Grey (CineEye) This is a great solution for a remote monitor for video shoots, and it's simple, no wires, no cables, and basically one-button operation. You install the app on your device (iOS or Android), connect the transmitter to your video camera (via HDMI), boot it up, then connect your device to it via WiFi. Launch the app and you're looking live at the video camera output. It delivers 1080p at 60fps and pushes audio to your device too. It's actually pretty awesome.

We gave it a real test in a room full of servers and a lot of potential electronic interference and it delivered a solid signal and connection up to about thirty feet. Beyond that it dropped a frame every now and then, but not bad.

If you're recording video through the app on your device, there's ten-minute limit per file, something to do with restrictions on the app's classification. That doesn't interfere with the camera recording video. It's just a file recording limit on whatever device you're monitoring the video on, if you choose to capture it while you view it.

The build quality is great. It feels practically indestructible. Battery life is solid.

If there is one thing to complain about, it's that the Android app is a bit blah. The iOS version is a lot better.
text_fidelity_b: Accsoon CineEye Video Transmitter, 5G Wireless Live Transmission to 4 Devices, 1080p WiFi HDMI, 100 Meter Range, Supports Android & iOS, RGB, 3D LUT Loading, Incredibly Low Latency – Grey (CineEye)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony HDR-PJ380/W High Definition Handycam Camcorder with 3.0-Inch LCD (White) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) While I'm quite comfortable using an SLR, I've not been all that handy with a camcorder in the past. It's been a few years since I used one, so I was curious to see if user-friendliness has kept pace with technological advancements.

With this model it has. I found it very easy to use right out of the box with just some minor trial and error. I did end up reading the manual (which is pretty decent) but the main functions were pretty self apparent by just fiddling around with it a bit. The menu structure is logical and well presented; the screen is clear and easy to view.

The overall build quality is excellent. It feels more substantial in hand than I expected at this price point while retaining a very lightweight and easy to carry profile. I like the button placement - feels very natural in hand.

I love having the internal memory for storage as well as the little touches, such as a built-in USB connector. These features help make this a grab-and-go type of device, which increases the likelihood and ease of bringing it along and capturing video. (Note: you can also use a plug-in memory card should you want to.)

The video quality in good light/outdoors is excellent - very sharp and clear. Low-light performance is a somewhat grainy but quite decent. Stills are pretty decent. It won't put an SLR to shame, but it's more than good enough for casual snapshots. The internal mic works well and is more immune to wind noise than I expected.

My only significant disappointment with the cam is the projector. Wonderful idea, but the actual performance is lackluster. The projected video is hard to see clearly if there's any appreciable amount of light in the room. The 100 inch projection spec is wildly optimistic if you expect to actually see what is being projected.

Given that this cam does everything else so well, is so easy to use, and a breeze to tote along, I won't detract any stars due to the shortcomings of the projector feature. This is a great cam for the novice cam user (such as myself) or even an intermediate user. However, if the projection feature is a primary need, this may not be a good cam for your needs.
text_fidelity_b: Sony HDR-PJ380/W High Definition Handycam Camcorder with 3.0-Inch LCD (White) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
ASUS ZenBook 13 Ultra-Slim Laptop, 13.3” Full HD WideView, 8th Gen Intel Core i5-8265U, 8GB LPDDR3, 512GB PCIe SSD, Backlit KB, Fingerprint, Slate Gray, Windows 10, UX331FA-AS51 This review is about what I think >90% of users will care about. The detail specs are a step further, higher and faster and advertised and advertised. The Asus ZenBook 13 has been my go-to everyday toting computer for some 7-8 years.

I have last year’s i5 gen7 ZenBook 13 to directly compare the two.

P.S. This Zen-book has been so good that I had it modified to incorpoarte medical practice compliant HIPA secured software. It's a step function increase in my nightly homework replacing my 7-year old Dell. This laptop is ubiquitously practical with 180 screen twist for descirbing patient procedures. With the med-system handshacks, its like 3x faster than the Dell.

First, this new i5 gen8 ZenBook 13 has a quarter inch all-around smaller footprint. The 1/4" is immediately noticeable from last year’s edition. The 1/4" bezel is noticeably better. As small a footprint as the two have, Asus has reduced the size with no compromise in keyboard utility.

This year's ZenBook is noticeably thinner. Recharge and headphone jack are reversed. This year's hinge is slightly more robust to account for the reduced thickness. The hinge has been a 'should improve' on ZenBooks since inception. This years may solve the issue for good.

The plug-outs are changed. Make sure the output ports are what you want. For my purposes, the addition of a standard HDMI vice last year’s mini-HDMI is an improvement requiring no adapter. Last year’s SD input has been correctly reduced to the increasingly popular/common micro-SD. Plug-out needs are easily resolved with a USB-C adapter hub.

The discrete Nvidia graphics will be an interesting exploration.

The Asus fingerprint reader has never failed. This edition looks identical to last years and has been creatively moved right and off the touchpad. The ZenBook has been the very best reader compared to my HP Envy (dang good) and Dell XPS (50:50 chance).

This year's battery is new tech. The lithium-polymer battery promises up to 14 hours and includes fast-charge technology that takes "just 49 minutes" to recharge to 60% capacity. I get 11 hours out of last year’s battery every day. I can't recall running out of battery on last years on battery save mode on trans-con flights.

Wish it came with Windows Pro instead of Home, but oh well.

Finally, both last years and this year are so fast you'd have to instrument to tell a speed difference. The ZenBooks 1-2-3 second boot to Windows is 'instant' for practical purposes.

Love it. Exceeds expectations. There's no purchase mistake to be made with the UX331.
text_fidelity_b: ASUS ZenBook 13 Ultra-Slim Laptop, 13.3” Full HD WideView, 8th Gen Intel Core i5-8265U, 8GB LPDDR3, 512GB PCIe SSD, Backlit KB, Fingerprint, Slate Gray, Windows 10, UX331FA-AS51

It feels sturdy and the keys have a pleasant texture. It's bigger than previous bluetooth keyboards I've tried, which I think is in keeping with it being designed to be used with multiple devices. It's also kind of heavy, so it seems more like an around the house keyboard than a portable.

I like it better as an occasional keyboard than one to use all the time. it's too flat to feel ergonomic. The alt and command keys on the bottom row are all double size, which feels like a designer wanted a big space bar but didn't want to leave any empty space anywhere. The result is that they are easy to bump, which can send you off into menus. The slot for standing up a device on the back of the keyboard feels a bit close, and not wide enough for my Surface tablet in landscape mode, and portrait mode makes it fall over, so the stand is likely only good for things up to small tablet size.

I used to get pretty good reception from an old aluminum christmas-tree type attic-mounted (non-amplified) antenna, but broke it accidentally. This amplified MANT940 is just as good, and a WHOLE lot smaller and easier to manipulate!

Attached to my Philips 5603D, this device (and 25 feet of extension cable) is providing me with 31 digital channels!?! Not always perfectly clearly (that is, there's occasional smear and freezing), but it's attached to an outside wall next to a window and easy to tweak - there's probably a better position, but this is convenient. So far I'm also getting 11 analog channels, but they're all dups. Some of the digital ones are pure advertising, and not all are HDTV, but WHOA - CBS! UNbelievable high def picture, and GREAT signal (WHYY sucks.) Beat THIS price, Comcast/FiOS!

BTW, I can now say most channels give great signal - even in a snowstorm!!!

Kinivo BTH220 Bluetooth Stereo Headphone – Supports Wireless Music Streaming and Hands-Free Calling I needed a cheap pair of bluetooth headphones for my Nexus for traveling, but didn't want to make too many compromises in favor of cost. These turned out quite well.

I was concerned about other reviews noting that the one-size-fits-all aspect of these headphones might be a problem with those with larger noggins (I am one of those people), but did not have any difficultly wearing these headphones - it fits with room to spare and parks securely around my ears.

The sound is decent - better than I expected given the price. I like that you can make volume adjustments with a push of a button on the right-ear side.

The headphones recharge via a USB port to your computer (or use the USB on any plug adapter that you may have for your other devices -- I used my Amazon Kindle plug adapter), with an indicator light changing from red to blue when it is fully charged. I'm not sure of the total battery life, but I've used them for six hours in a single stretch, and they still were going strong.

I also tried walking around and away from my Nexus 7, and the headphones still worked fine. I didn't test the absolute limit of its range, but I got a good 20 feet away on the same floor without a problem.

The sound and build quality won't knock your socks off, but for the price, it's a great performer. Definitely recommend this as if you're looking for a good value in a bluetooth headphone.

text_fidelity_a:
PANASONIC Wings Sport Headphones are Ultra-Light Wireless Bluetooth Sport Earbud 3D Flex Sport Clips with Microphone and Call/Volume Controller, IPX5 Rated Water-Resistant - RP-BTS35-K (Black) I received these earphones from Amazon Vine in early January, 2018. I liked the over-the-ears design. It makes the earphones far less likely to fall off when exercising. The sound quality is also excellent. I found its wireless bluetooth function quite handy for listening to music on my smartphone while walking, biking, lifting weights or doing calisthenics.

In short, as long as the battery could be charged, these sport earphones worked quite well. But suddenly, a few weeks ago, after only 7 months of use, the battery simply would no longer take a charge. The manual says that the battery should last through up to 300 charges, and there is absolutely no way that in only seven months I charged this device 300 times. It holds a charge well while the battery is working, much better than the other bluetooth earbuds that I have owned. So I could use it for up to five days without charging the battery. This means that, in seven months, I only charged the battery about 42-50 times, at most. This means the life of the battery was a mere 16% of what the manufacturer promised!

This is not a device in which the battery can be replaced. Therefore, once the battery dies, the earphones are worthless. Since the warranty is only for 90 days, there is no recourse with the manufacturer for replacing this device after that length of time.

The way that this product works is a good idea, but until the design includes the possibility of replacing the battery, the high price is simply not worth it. I will have to stick to cheap earbuds which are not such a hit to my pocketbook when their non-replaceable battery dies.

I rate this product as follows:

Sound quality 5 stars
Durability of battery: 1 star
Value for price: 1 star
Overall average: 2.3 stars
text_fidelity_b: PANASONIC Wings Sport Headphones are Ultra-Light Wireless Bluetooth Sport Earbud 3D Flex Sport Clips with Microphone and Call/Volume Controller, IPX5 Rated Water-Resistant - RP-BTS35-K (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
RCA BRC10GR Bathroom Clock Radio (Green) Updated review:

I've become somewhat dependent on the sight of this bright blue radio. Every morning I stumble, groggy-eyed, into my bathroom. Having this clear-sounding radio, blasting my favorite music, is a nice pick-me-up as I shower. But does the design offer me anything more than what I would expect from a typical shower radio?

PROS: It's cleverly designed to mimic the shape of a shampoo. It melds easily into the background. My initial fear was that I would accidentally grab it instead of the real thing, but so far that hasn't happened.

PROS: The sound quality is tinny but quite decent for a shower radio.

PROS: The radio offers a "store" function where you can bookmark your favorite radio stations and get to them fast by using a "recall" button. This is a feature common to most clock radios but I don't spend enough time in the bathroom to use it. I basically stick to one station while showering and can't see myself using the "store" function unless I'm taking a long bath. Still, nice to have that option.

PROS: Great battery life! I used my AA batteries for this and it has been running for months with no problem.

CONS: It's not that easy to see the buttons. They're located on the sides of the device but the positions are not intuitive. I always have to squint a little to see the print above the buttons because the buttons do not stick out.

CONS: "Light up" function. The time display is very clear and easy to read as-is. Since it's not a bedtime clock radio that benefits from having a glow-in-the-dark function, this feature feels extraneous to me. Perhaps it's best for someone who likes to take a bath with candles all around.

CONS: Not space saving. I used to have a shower radio that could be hooked over the showerhead. While the radio is not huge, I still had to move my shampoo and conditioner bottles to make room for it.

Overall it is a decent radio and I have been using it since I got it with no problems.
text_fidelity_b: RCA BRC10GR Bathroom Clock Radio (Green)
